# entrepot_repository_signing_key (Resource)

Imports your own OpenPGP private key as the signing key of a hosted `apt` or `yum` repository (by default the server generates one on first use). The repository metadata is re-signed with the imported key.

**Drift:** the private key is write-only. The provider computes the key's fingerprint locally and compares it with the server's active key on every refresh; if the key was rotated or replaced outside Terraform, the plan shows a `fingerprint` change and applying it imports the configured key again.

**Destroy** rotates the key: the server replaces the imported key with a freshly generated one (a repository always has a signing key), so clients must fetch the new public key.

The private key (and passphrase) are stored in the Terraform state; protect it accordingly.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "entrepot_repository" "apt" {
  name       = "apt-internal"
  format     = "apt"
  kind       = "hosted"
  blob_store = "default"
}

# Sign the repository with your own key instead of a server-generated one:
#   gpg --armor --export-secret-keys <key-id> > signing-key.asc
resource "entrepot_repository_signing_key" "apt" {
  repository  = entrepot_repository.apt.name
  private_key = file("${path.module}/signing-key.asc")
  passphrase  = var.signing_key_passphrase
}

variable "signing_key_passphrase" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  default   = null
}

output "apt_key_fingerprint" {
  value = entrepot_repository_signing_key.apt.fingerprint
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) ASCII-armored OpenPGP private key (`gpg --armor --export-secret-keys <id>`) containing exactly one key with a usable signing (sub)key. Write-only: changes on the server are detected through `fingerprint`. Null after import until the next apply records it.
- `repository` (String) Name of a hosted `apt` or `yum` repository. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `passphrase` (String, Sensitive) Passphrase of a protected private key. The server stores the key decrypted (sealed with its secrets key), so changing only the passphrase makes no API call.

### Read-Only

- `algorithm` (String) Key algorithm, e.g. `rsa4096` or `ed25519`.
- `created_at` (String) When the active key was imported or generated (RFC 3339).
- `fingerprint` (String) Fingerprint (upper-case hex) of the repository's active key.
- `id` (String) Same as `repository`.
- `public_key` (String) ASCII-armored public key to install on clients.
- `url` (String) URL from which clients download the public key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Signing keys are imported by repository name. The private key cannot be
# read back: the next apply records the configured key (no API call when it
# matches the active key's fingerprint).
terraform import entrepot_repository_signing_key.apt apt-internal
```
